clauses.requirement: In the photometry of retro-reflection (Annex 5 Part 1, para 4 measurement precautions, with best practice per the relevant CIE reports and standards), the precautions on residual and stray light given in para 4.1 shall be considered when measuring the rear retro-reflector.

Because very low light levels are measured, precautions shall minimise stray light errors: the background to the sample and the sample holder framework should be matt black, and the field of view of the photometer head and the spread of light from both the sample and the source shall be restricted as much as possible.
Reflections from the floor and walls occurring over the relatively long test distances shall be screened from both the sample and the photometer head by baffles.

Residual stray light shall always be corrected for by measuring it with the sample covered by an opaque matt black surface, zigzag folded black paper of the same size and shape, or a specular black surface suitably oriented with a light trap; this value shall be subtracted from the value measured on the retro-reflective device.
In the photometry of retro-reflection, the apparatus stability precautions of para 4.2 shall be considered (best practice per the relevant CIE reports and standards).

The light source and photometer head should remain stable throughout the test period; as photometer head sensitivity and V(λ) adaptation change with temperature, laboratory ambient temperature should not vary significantly during testing; sufficient time should be allowed for the apparatus to stabilise before measurements begin.
To check the overall stability of the reflex photometer during a series of tests, periodic measurements of RI values of a stable reference standard should be made.

The goniometer used for retro-reflection measurements in the CIE geometry shall be as defined in paragraph 2.3 of the Regulation and illustrated in Figure A4-II (photometer head O arbitrarily shown vertically above source I; first axis fixed, horizontal and perpendicular to the observation half-plane); any equivalent arrangement of the components may be used.
